title: AWS CWI Training in North Charleston, SC: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Lowcountry ship repair, aerospace, auto plant and steel welders: corporate, online or one-to-one. Parts A, B and C covered.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in North Charleston, South Carolina: Six Days for Lowcountry Ship Repair, Aerospace and Plant Welding Inspectors
html:
North Charleston is where much of the Lowcountry's heavy industry meets the water. Ships go into dry dock beside the Cooper River, wide-body jets roll out of the Boeing site next to the airport, vans and cars leave body shops in Ladson and Ridgeville, and a steel mill in Huger rolls sheet and structural steel. Welding runs through every one of those operations, and so does the need for people who can inspect it against a code and put their name on the record. For people heading toward that role, Atlantis NDT offers a six-day (6-day) course that prepares them for all three parts of the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination: Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. Lowcountry candidates can take it as a corporate course at their employer's facility, as online study with an instructor answering their questions, or as six days of one-to-one sessions. AWS administers the exam, sets the eligibility rules and awards the certification, while Atlantis teaches the material and certifies nobody. There is no Atlantis classroom in North Charleston, and nothing is taught at a local venue; Atlantis keeps offices in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India. To start, send a North Charleston CWI exam prep enquiry.

How the six days fit a Lowcountry candidate

The course follows the structure of the exam. Two days build the Fundamentals that Part A tests: processes and terminology, joint design, welding symbols, metallurgy, mechanical testing, discontinuities and their causes, NDT methods, math, safety and the inspector's responsibilities. One day rehearses the Part B practical with real gauges and procedure documents, one day works inside the code you have picked for Part C, one day is timed practice papers, and the last day returns to weak areas and the steps between you and exam day. The AWS CWI exam prep course page sets out every block.

Corporate delivery for a plant, yard or fabricator

An employer with a group to prepare can have the six days delivered at its own facility, using its own welds, gauges and, where it fits, its own code and procedures. That suits a ship repair yard bringing several leading hands into QA, or a supplier building an in-house inspection team for a customer audit.

Online study for individuals

Individuals follow a study plan built on the six-day outline, with course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers. An instructor answers questions as they come up. There are no set class times, which matters in a region where many people work rotating plant shifts or long days when a ship is in dock.

One-to-one for a single candidate

Six days of one-to-one sessions give one person the instructor's full attention, online or in person at a location agreed when booking. It is the option for someone who wants the pace set entirely around their own gaps.

North Charleston's welding economy, sector by sector

Within a short drive of each other the metro area holds shipyards, an aircraft plant, vehicle plants and a steel mill. Each sector uses welding differently, and each points toward a different Part C choice.

Ship repair at Detyens Shipyards

Detyens Shipyards, founded in 1962 and now run by the family's third generation, repairs ships at 1670 Drydock Avenue in North Charleston. The yard lists three graving docks that take vessels up to Panamax size, the largest measuring 751 by 134 feet, plus a floating dock for smaller craft, more than 8,000 feet of deepwater pier with rail access, and eight portal gantry cranes alongside four tower cranes. Its customers include the U.S. Navy and Military Sealift Command, under overhaul contracts for USNS ships, as well as commercial, government and research vessel owners. Steel, tank and pipe repairs are core services, so welding inspection sits in the middle of nearly every job: renewing plate and stiffeners, repairing tanks and piping, and checking each repair weld before the vessel floats out.

Aerospace at Boeing South Carolina

Boeing South Carolina fabricates, assembles and delivers the 787-8, 787-9 and 787-10 in North Charleston, with a second campus in Orangeburg. In November 2025 Boeing broke ground on a new final assembly building of about 1.2 million square feet, roughly the size of the existing one, together with a parts preparation facility, a vertical fin paint facility, additional flight line stalls and a larger Interiors Responsibility Center, and it targeted a 787 production rate of ten aircraft a month in 2026. The 787 airframe is built largely from composite structure joined with fasteners, so a welding inspector around an aircraft program is more likely to deal with tooling, fixtures, ground support equipment, facility piping and metal suppliers than with the airframe itself. Suppliers that fusion-weld aerospace hardware often work to AWS D17.1, one of the Part C options.

The expansion is also a construction job in its own right. Boeing says a joint venture of HITT and BE&K Building Group is leading the work, with more than 2,500 construction workers expected on site. Its structural steel is welded and inspected like that of any large industrial building, mostly to AWS D1.1.

Vans and cars in Ladson and Ridgeville

Two vehicle plants sit within a short drive of North Charleston. Mercedes-Benz Vans builds the Sprinter and eSprinter in Ladson, where the plant was upgraded for body manufacturing and painting. Volvo Cars builds the EX90 at its plant in Ridgeville, in Berkeley County, and has invested there in an upgraded body shop, an upgraded paint shop and a battery pack assembly line. Vehicle body shops rely mostly on robotic resistance spot welding, with arc welding on brackets, frames, subassemblies and tooling. A CWI in that world usually works in quality or supplier quality: auditing suppliers' welding, checking arc-welded parts and reviewing process records. The automotive spot-welding specifications are not a Part C option, so automotive candidates generally take D1.1, or D1.2 where aluminum is the main material.

Steelmaking at Nucor Steel Berkeley

Nucor Steel Berkeley in Huger is a sheet and structural steel mill. Nucor describes it as able to produce up to 3.5 million tons a year of flat-rolled and structural steel, with about 1,000 employees, serving markets from construction and energy to automotive and heavy equipment. A mill generates steady maintenance and repair welding on equipment, structures and handling gear, and its products feed the fabricators that build warehouses, plants and bridges across the region.

Port, logistics and construction steel

The Port of Charleston's terminals, the distribution centers along the interstate corridors and the industrial parks around the airport keep structural steel moving through regional fabricators and erectors. Most of that work is welded to AWS D1.1, and larger projects call for documented welding inspection in the shop and in the field. Bridge and interchange steel built for the South Carolina Department of Transportation follows AWS D1.5.

Who hires welding inspectors around North Charleston

  • Ship repair yards and their subcontractors. Repair contracts for government and commercial owners need inspectors who can track welder qualifications, verify fit-up and accept repairs against the owner's specification.
  • Aerospace suppliers and tooling shops. Companies supplying the aircraft program with fixtures, ground equipment and fusion-welded metal parts need inspectors comfortable with tight dimensional control and customer specifications.
  • Automotive suppliers. Firms making welded frames, brackets and assemblies for the vehicle plants use CWIs in quality and supplier-quality roles.
  • Structural steel fabricators and erectors. Shops supplying warehouses, plants and bridges need in-house QC against D1.1 or D1.5, and customers increasingly ask to see a named, qualified inspector on the quality plan.
  • Inspection and testing firms. Third-party firms place welding inspectors and NDT technicians on construction projects and at fabricators for owners and engineers.

Lowcountry employers often want an inspector who can cross sectors, because a single industrial park might hold a tooling shop, a structural fabricator and an automotive supplier side by side.

Choosing the Part C code for Lowcountry work

Part C lets you keep one code book open, and AWS lets you choose which. Alongside D1.1 and API 1104, AWS offers D1.2 for aluminum, D1.5 for bridges, D15.1 for railcars and locomotives, D17.1 for aerospace fusion welding, an ASME package of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. Here is how those options line up with the region's work:

If you mostly work inA sensible Part C bookWhat you will be tested on
Ship repair structure, warehouses, plants and general fabricationAWS D1.1Prequalified joints, qualification, fabrication tolerances and visual acceptance for steel
Fusion-welded aerospace parts and tooling built to aerospace specificationsAWS D17.1Aerospace weld classes, qualification and acceptance requirements
Aluminum structures and vehicle componentsAWS D1.2Structural welding of aluminum and its qualification rules
Shipboard piping, plant utilities and power pipingASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Procedure and welder qualification variables, plus piping examination and acceptance
Highway bridges and interchangesAWS D1.5Bridge fabrication, qualification and inspection requirements

AWS fixes the edition of each book used in the exam, and it is not always the newest one on the shelf, so check your application before you buy a copy. For background, see AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5, ASME Section IX and the D1.1 acceptance criteria guide.

The AWS South Carolina Section and the Lowcountry welding pipeline

Welding professionals in the Charleston area meet through the AWS South Carolina Section, which belongs to AWS District 5. Its recent calendar has included a New Year social in Charleston in early 2026, sponsored by a laser equipment supplier and run partly as a fundraiser. For CWI candidates the section is worth the evening: it is where you meet QC managers and working inspectors, learn which employers are adding inspection staff, and find people who can vouch for the welding experience you will list on the AWS application.

Many Lowcountry inspectors learned to weld at Trident Technical College, which offers an Associate in Applied Science in welding covering current and conventional techniques, metals science and technical drawing. The college lists AWS SENSE Level I and Level II accreditation for the program, NCCER-certified trainers and authorization as a Department of Transportation welder training facility. Others came through shipyard work, military service at Joint Base Charleston or plant maintenance crews. Any of those routes can support a CWI application, because AWS counts recognized education toward part of the experience requirement and wants the experience itself documented and verifiable. Trident and the other programs here are part of the region's own pipeline and have no connection to Atlantis.

Booking the CWI exam from North Charleston

AWS QC1, the 2016 edition with its amendment, governs the examination. You need a score of at least 72% on each of the three parts, and AWS issues one consolidated score report. Part A is 150 fundamentals questions. Part B pairs hands-on tasks, done with tools and specimens AWS provides, with 46 questions. Part C is open book, around 50 to 65 questions on the code you selected.

The two computer-based parts, A and C, are booked through Prometric with the eligibility code that comes in your AWS confirmation letter, at a Prometric test center convenient to you. Part B is the one to plan early. AWS gives the practical only at its own seminar and examination locations, on dates it sets, so check the current AWS schedule for the nearest session in the Southeast; if nothing is close, the practical means a trip, and it should be booked around your plant or yard calendar. AWS publishes its examination fees on aws.org. To budget the whole effort, including travel and time off, use the CWI exam cost planner.

Studying around line rates, plant shifts and dock periods

Lowcountry work patterns vary by sector. Vehicle and aircraft plants run on production rates and rotating shifts, with overtime when a line is pushing to hit its numbers. Ship repair is lumpy: a vessel arrives, the yard works flat out until it floats out, and then the pace drops until the next one. Construction follows project milestones and the summer heat. Whatever your pattern, the online format lets you take the fundamentals blocks in quieter weeks and hold the timed practice papers for the run-up to your Prometric appointments.

Two habits help any Part C candidate here. Keep your code book where you work and look up the clauses behind the joints you see each day, whether that is a doubler on a hull or a column splice on a warehouse frame. And practise Part B measurement with real gauges on scrap and cut-outs until you trust your readings. Between shifts, the Practical NDT welding workshop simulator offers browser-based rehearsal of inspection steps.

Corporate: six days at a Lowcountry employer's facility

Corporate delivery brings the full six days to the employer's own premises. The practical day uses the company's fillet gauges, bridge cam gauges, hi-lo gauges and real welds, from welder test coupons to production rejects, so the measurement practice matches what those inspectors accept every day. The code day can be split when a group is mixed: a yard might send structural people toward D1.1 and pipe people toward the ASME package, while an aerospace supplier might want D17.1 for most of its group.

Scheduling is usually built around the employer's own peaks, such as a dry-docking, a model changeover or a customer audit. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually, meets the experience and vision rules individually and books their own exam. The employer can organize and support; it cannot apply on anyone's behalf.

One-to-one sessions for a North Charleston candidate

For a single person, the one-to-one format provides six days of sessions with the instructor, online or in person at a location agreed when booking. It suits a supplier-quality engineer who knows the paperwork but needs hands-on measurement practice, a structural welder whose code reading needs work, or someone leaving military service at Joint Base Charleston who wants a civilian inspection credential. Because there is no group to keep pace with, the sessions go wherever that candidate is weakest.

Eligibility and the vision record for Lowcountry applicants

The years of welding-related experience AWS asks for depend on your schooling: five with a high school diploma, as little as one with a welding engineering or welding technology degree, and longer for anyone with less formal education. The work must involve welded products, such as fabrication, production, repair, construction or inspection, and it has to be verifiable; AWS makes the final call. You also need a current AWS Visual Acuity Record showing near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without glasses, and a color perception test, completed by a qualified practitioner within the window AWS allows before your exam. If you are short on years, the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) is an earlier step. The full table is on the CWI exam prep course page; for the wider picture read the CWI requirements and career guide.

After the CWI: career paths around North Charleston

The CWI stays valid for nine years, with renewals filed at the third and sixth years and recertification at the ninth. From there, Lowcountry inspectors tend to branch in three directions.

  • Senior roles. Inspectors who go on to run a supplier's or contractor's welding quality program often aim for the AWS Senior CWI; see the Senior CWI pathway. Additional AWS endorsements widen the codes you are recognized on.
  • NDT methods. Aerospace and ship repair both lean on penetrant, magnetic particle and ultrasonic testing. Performing those methods needs training, logged experience and certification by your employer under its written practice. Atlantis runs SNT-TC-1A-based courses in VT, MT, PT and UT; see NDT training in North Charleston, aerospace NDT training in North Charleston, PT Level 2 and VT Level 2. The Practical NDT simulator page for North Charleston explains how simulator practice fits alongside.
  • Owner-side and third-party inspection. Experienced CWIs move into owner's representative and source inspection roles on construction and marine projects.

To compare the main inspection credentials, read CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II and welding inspector vs NDT technician. For local testing services, see ultrasonic testing in Charleston and magnetic particle testing in Charleston.

Other Southeast CWI pages and a North Charleston quote

Candidates elsewhere in the region can read the CWI exam prep pages for Charlotte, Atlanta, Jacksonville and Norfolk.

For a quote, say whether the course is for you alone or for a group and which format suits, outline each candidate's schooling and welding background, note the Part C book each one has in mind, and for corporate delivery give the facility location, the gauges and sample welds on hand and any production peaks to avoid. Use the North Charleston CWI enquiry form.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in North Charleston?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in North Charleston and no local venue. Lowcountry candidates take the six-day course online with instructor support, as one-to-one sessions online or in person at a location agreed when booking, or as a corporate course at their employer's facility. See the outline.

The American Welding Society. AWS administers the examination, grades it and issues the CWI to candidates who pass. Atlantis prepares candidates; AWS has not approved, accredited or endorsed the course.

faq.q: I build tooling and ground equipment for the aircraft program. Which Part C code fits?
faq.a: If your work is fusion-welded to aerospace specifications, AWS D17.1 is the closest match. If most of what you weld is steel structure, frames and fixtures built to structural drawings, AWS D1.1 is usually the more practical choice.

faq.q: Which code should a ship repair welder at Detyens or a similar yard choose?
faq.a: Structural repair people usually take AWS D1.1, the nearest AWS match to plate, stiffener and foundation work. Pipe and machinery people often prefer the ASME package of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3. See AWS D1.1.

faq.q: Where do North Charleston candidates take the exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based and booked through Prometric using the eligibility code from AWS. AWS holds Part B, the practical, only where and when it schedules a session, so find the closest Southeast date on the AWS schedule and arrange travel early.

faq.q: Can an automotive supplier have the course delivered at its plant?
faq.a: Yes. In the corporate format the instructor works through the six days at your plant, using your own gauges and production welds. Automotive groups usually prepare for D1.1, or D1.2 where aluminum dominates. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually. Send an enquiry.

faq.q: Is one-to-one available in person in the Charleston area?
faq.a: Yes. A single candidate can book six days of sessions with the instructor in person, at a place agreed at the time of booking, or take the same sessions online. There is no Atlantis classroom in the area, so the place is set for each booking.

faq.q: Are the practice questions real AWS exam questions?
faq.a: No. All practice questions and timed papers are original, written by Atlantis against the topic areas AWS publishes. Atlantis does not see the AWS examination.

faq.q: Does military welding experience count toward the CWI?
faq.a: It can, if it involved welding-related work on welded products and you can document it with dates, duties and someone who can verify it. AWS decides what counts. The required years depend on your education; see CWI requirements.

faq.q: What NDT training can I add after the CWI?
faq.a: Atlantis trains technicians in VT, MT, PT and UT on courses built around ASNT SNT-TC-1A; certification then comes from your employer under its written practice. See NDT training in North Charleston and aerospace NDT training.
